_comment: The discovery journal (ADR 0061): the Discoveries tab of the progression book. Each kind lists its entries from other data, so new biomes, landforms, animals, stones and ore veins appear without code changes. from: biomes (biomes.json, skipping tags in skip_tags, or only those with one of only_tags), landforms (biomes.json "landforms", part B), mobs (mobs.json species), items (items.json items carrying any of tags), ore_veins (ore_veins.json veins), list (the names in entries). An entry's line is texts["kind:name"], else the source's "lore", else the kind's text with %s = the display name. icon = an item id for the toast and the tab; an entry's own icon from icons["kind:name"]. Reward: the entry alone (the developer's call, 2026-10-25).

kinds.title: Caves
kinds.text: You first went down into a %s.

kinds.title: Ore veins
kinds.text: Your pick rang on a %s vein.

texts.biome:plains: Open grass to the horizon, wild wheat and carrots in the hollows. Sheep graze here.
texts.biome:forest: Oak and birch over leaf litter, mushrooms at the roots, berries in the clearings.
texts.biome:old_growth_forest: Trees older than any village, trunks thick as a hut, and the floor dark under them.
texts.biome:taiga: Spruce and cold air; the ground stays hard well into spring.
texts.biome:desert: Sand and heat. Water is worth more than copper here.
texts.biome:mountains: Bare rock and thin air. The veins run closer to the surface where the land is torn open.
texts.biome:swamp: Black water between the roots. Clay lies under the mud.
texts.biome:beach: Sand, shells and driftwood where the land gives up.
texts.biome:birch_forest: White trunks in cool air, light falling through to ferns and berries.
texts.biome:flower_meadow: Grass and flowers as far as you can see. The bees found it first.
texts.biome:volcanic: Black rock, glassy cliffs and no shade. The mountain is still warm underfoot.
texts.biome:mangrove: Trees standing in the tide on mud and clay, reeds between the roots.
texts.landmark:ruin: Old walls of someone who came before. Their pots may still hold something.
texts.landmark:cave: The dark under the hills. Ore shows in the walls where the rock is open.
texts.landmark:waterfall: A river falling over a cliff, loud enough to hide your steps.
texts.landmark:aquifer: Still water in the rock: a vein of the world. Open it and it pours; follow it down to its spring stone.
texts.landmark:magma_conduit: Still lava in a tube through the rock. Breach it from above only. Its heart lies deeper.
texts.landmark:spring_stone: The head of an aquifer: a chamber of water round a blue stone.
texts.landmark:magma_heart: The heart of a magma conduit, in a bath of lava. The hottest thing under the hills.
texts.landmark:river: Running water: fish, clay on the banks, and a road for anyone with a boat.
texts.landmark:lake: Still water. Good land for a farm, close enough to carry water.
texts.animal:sheep: Wool and mutton. They follow wheat.
texts.animal:pig: Meat and hide. They follow carrots.
texts.animal:chicken: Eggs every few minutes and feathers for arrows.
texts.animal:bear: Strong, fast and short-tempered. Leave it be, or bring a spear.
texts.animal:gloam_hound: Night hunters in packs of up to three. They run down sheep and deer, and you, if you are alone in the dark.
texts.animal:crow: Flocks wheel over fields and forests. They come down for scattered seed and scatter at a step.
texts.animal:salmon: Shoals in cold rivers and lakes. Quick to scatter, good to eat.
texts.animal:jellyfish: They drift in warm seas and sting what brushes them: a few seconds of poison.
texts.landmark:abandoned_mine: Rusted rails and rotten props lead into the rock: someone dug here before you.
texts.phenomenon:steam: Water over lava or a fire boils to steam, which rises, fills a sealed room and raises its pressure, and condenses back to water where it cools.
texts.phenomenon:toxic_gas: Toxic sludge boils into a heavy green gas that sinks and pools in low caves. Do not breathe it.
texts.animal:cave_salamander: Pale and slow, it lives on the wet floors of lush, fungal, dripstone and frozen caves.
texts.animal:songbird: Small birds that flit from branch to ground to branch, and sing at dawn.
texts.animal:goat: Sure-footed on rocky slopes. Lure one with wheat or carrots; a clay bowl milks it, and it refills as it grazes.
texts.landmark:abandoned_camp: A cold fire ring and a rotten bedroll: someone camped here and did not come back.
texts.critter:glow_worm: Threads of light hang from moss and vines on cave ceilings.
texts.critter:firefly: Sparks that drift over grass on warm nights.
